newsitem.title: USA: Judge issues injuction to block Proposition 209.
newsitem.headline: Judge issues injuction to block Proposition 209.

text.p: A federal judge on Monday granted a preliminary injunction blocking Proposition 209, an initiative that would roll back affirmative action programmes in California.

The injunction, handed down by U.S. District Judge Thelton Henderson of San Francisco, bars Gov. Pete Wilson and California Attorney General Dan Lungren from implementing Proposition 209, which was passed by voters in November, until the judge resolves the dispute over its constitutionality.

In his 67-page ruling, Henderson said opponents of the initiative had demonstrated the "probability of success on their claim that Proposition 209 violates the Fourteenth Amendment's equal protection guarantee to full participation in the political life of the community."
Civil rights groups challenging the constitutionality of the initiative said the ruling was a major victory.
"We're elated. Our position has been vindicated," said attorney Edward Chen of the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) of northern California. "This freezes everything for the foreseeable future."
Backers of the initiative denounced the decision.
"The American system of government is being severely tested," said Ward Connerly, a black California businessman who led the campaign for the initiative.

"While I maintain an abiding faith in our system of checks and balances, the decision of Judge Thelton Henderson to issue a preliminary injunction against Proposition 209 shakes the very foundation of our system," he said.
Lungren was expected to appeal the order.

Californians voted 54-46 percent on Nov. 5 to make Proposition 209 part of the state constitution. It would bar discrimination and preferential treatment based on race or sex in public employment, education and contracting in California.
The initiative, the first of its kind passed by any state, would eliminate most California affirmative action programmes designed to create opportunities for women and racial minorities.
On Friday the White House said the Justice Department had concluded that the California initiative was unconstitutional, and would back legal action to overturn it.
